There is more to consider here than a simple binary split between people who "have" and "don't have" an internal monologue. I believe a much more useful conceptualization is to organize it into a hierarchy, which would go something like this:

  • Level 1: Has no capability for internal monologue, must literally speak out loud to reason.
  • Level 2: Can think internally, but only in a very deliberate manner, essentially emulating speech (subvocalization).
  • Level 3: Is capable of abstract internal thought, but it is highly disorganized or chatters nonstop in a nonlinear stream of consciousness. (This level is highly correlated with mental illness and leftism)
  • Level 4: Is capable of abstract internal thought, and is capable of controlling the flow of thought: turning it on and off, directing it, silencing it. May not have mastered converting abstract thoughts into words readily. (Most people require meditation to approach this level.)
  • Level 5: Abstract internal thought becomes the native mode of conceptualization, to the point where words are unnecessary a great deal of the time. Has mastered the ability to convert abstract thought into linear expression via deliberate thought and speech. Can synthesize new connections and concepts that would never occur to individuals who are bound by using words and pre-established definitions to reason.

Now I just pulled most of this out of my ass, but it's an example of how there is much more to this topic than most are considering. Level 2 is probably better off than level 3 for all practical intents, since the lack of abstract thought is better than untamed chaos in one's mind. Level 5 is unlikely to think in words most of the time, so they may (inaccurately) describe themselves as "having no internal monologue," but of course they can do so on demand when necessary. And so you get a horseshoe phenomenon, with both the very stupid and very intelligent claiming to have no monologue.

This probably isn't some kind of progression that people can generally "level up" in. It's determined by racial genetics and IQ with only a bit of wiggle room for individual effort.
